statement: Let count(v) be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v, and for a finite set S of integers let W(S) = sum_{v in S} v * count(v). The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = max { W(S) | S is a finite set of integers such that (a) for every v in S, count(v) > 0, and (b) for every integer v, not (v in S and v+1 in S) }.
preconditions: nums is a nonempty slice of 64-bit signed integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 20000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10000. All arithmetic below is mathematical, identifying each nums[i] and the returned i64 value with its integer value.
